subject.title: Browser tool: 7 improvements from real-world automation field test

question: Which remaining #44431 browser-tool contract should OpenClaw sponsor first after the shipped selector, wait, delay, and batch groundwork?
rationale: The unresolved requests require choosing a model-facing browser API and profile support boundary, not just filling in a missing implementation detail.

options.title: Prioritize state and blocker signals
options.body: Create focused work for stale refs, readiness/manual-blocker reporting, and post-action verification, then align schema, skill guidance, docs, and live proof around that contract.

options.title: Expose batch model-facing first
options.body: Resolve the current managed-runtime versus provider-schema gap by deciding whether and how batch actions should be advertised to models across supported profiles.

options.title: Defer CDP and CAPTCHA surfaces
options.body: Leave inspectElement/event-listener and CAPTCHA signaling as later or plugin-owned work until the core/browser contract has a clear owner and safety model.

recommendation.title: Prioritize state and blocker signals
recommendation.body: Create focused work for stale refs, readiness/manual-blocker reporting, and post-action verification, then align schema, skill guidance, docs, and live proof around that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently merged the related browser batch/selector contract work and touched the central route and typing surfaces.
